}}'''Sir Simon Fraser Campbell''' (born 27 March 1941) is a British [[chemist]].<ref name=nrd/>

==Early life and education==
Campbell was born on 27 March 1941 in [[Lapal]], [[England]].<ref name="RSC2006">{{cite web | title=Dr Simon Campbell receives CBE at Buckingham Palace | website=Royal Society of Chemistry | date=14 December 2006 | url=https://www.rsc.org/news-events/articles/2006/12-december/simon-campbell-cbe/ | access-date=14 January 2023}}</ref> He obtained a first-class [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] degree in [[Chemistry]] in 1962, a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in 1965, and an [[honorary degree|honorary]] [[Doctor of Science|DSc]] degree in 2004 from the [[University of Birmingham]].

==Career==
Campbell was President of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] from 2004 to 2006.<ref name=nrd>{{Cite journal |pmid = 16918018 |year = 2006 |last1 = Campbell |first1 = S |title = Simon Campbell CBE, FMed ''Sci'', FRS. Interview by Joanna Owens |journal = Nature Reviews Drug Discovery |volume = 5 |issue = 8 |pages = 626 |doi = 10.1038/nrd2116 |s2cid = 38734548 |doi-access = free}}</ref> He led innovative research, discovering some of the world's best-selling prescription drugs, including [[sildenafil]], [[amlodipine]], and [[doxazosin]].<ref name="RPS2014">{{cite journal |title=Scientist who developed Viagra receives knighthood in New Year’s Honours |journal=The Pharmaceutical Journal |publisher=Royal Pharmaceutical Society |year=2014 |issn=2053-6186 |doi=10.1211/pj.2014.20067494 |url=https://pharmaceutical-journal.com/article/news/scientist-who-developed-viagra-receives-knighthood-in-new-years-honours|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He was visiting lecturer at [[Universidade de São Paulo]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 October 2010 |title=MMV ESAC member in Times Top 100 Scientists |url=https://www.mmv.org/newsroom/news-resources-search/mmv-esac-member-times-top-100-scientists |access-date=21 July 2026 |website=Medicines for Malaria Venture}}</ref> and a medicinal chemist for Pfizer.<ref>{{cite web|author=Simon Campbell C.B.E F.R.S Ph.D. |url=http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=693816&privcapId=156645&previousCapId=1318957&previousTitle=Chroma%20Therapeutics%20Ltd |title=Astex Therapeutics Limited: Private Company Information - BusinessWeek |publisher=Investing.businessweek.com |access-date=2011-12-01}}{{dead link|date=April 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Campbell was also visiting professor at [[University of Leeds]], and served on the advisory board of [[University of Kent]], and [[University of Bristol]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/c/20688/Simon%20Fraser+CAMPBELL.aspx |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120728175436/http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/c/20688/Simon%20Fraser+CAMPBELL.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-07-28 |title=Dr Simon Campbell, CBE, FRS, FMedSci Authorised Biography – Debrett's People of Today, Dr Simon Campbell, CBE, FRS, FMedSci Profile |publisher=Debretts.com |date=1941-03-27 |access-date=2011-12-01 }}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Campbell was [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] in the [[2015 New Year Honours]] for services to chemistry,<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=61092 |supp=y|page=N2|date=31 December 2014}}</ref><ref>[https://www.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/391413/New_Year_Honours_List_2015.pdf 2015 New Year Honours List]</ref> having previously been made a [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE). He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1999<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sir Simon Campbell CBE FMedSci FRS |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/simon-campbell-11182/ |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=The Royal Society |language=en}}</ref> and of the [[Academy of Medical Sciences (United Kingdom)|Academy of Medical Sciences]] in 2003.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sir Simon Campbell CBE FRS FMedSci |url=https://acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/fellow/Simon%20Fraser-Campbell-0033z00002qIIZVAA4 |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=Academy of Medical Sciences}}</ref>
